design.additiveWrapper: renderConsumerDiagnosticsDistribution(contract, distributionVersion) calls renderVersionedActionSdkDistribution, parses the manifest text it returned, and re-emits it with exactly two added keys; the generated module bytes are passed through unchanged and the P08 generator is not touched
design.diagnosticsDigest: sha256 over JSON.stringify({schemaVersion:1, distributionVersion, coordinate, integrity, diagnosticsPath, diagnosticsSource}) in that key order. It records the shipped runner's exact bytes next to the payload that carries it, separately from manifest.integrity. Both the digest and the runner it covers travel inside the same payload, so the digest is a drift record, not a trust anchor
design.shippedRunner: diagnose.mjs, embedded in the generator via String.raw, ESM, node builtins only (node:crypto, node:fs/promises, node:path), no repository path, no relative import, no subprocess and no network
design.failClosed: every refusal exits 1, writes nothing to stdout and emits exactly one CONSUMER_DIAGNOSTICS_ERROR:<CODE> line at the start of a stderr line, always before the generated module is evaluated; the healthy path exits 0, is silent on stderr and prints one deterministic JSON report that leaks no host path

claims.supersededClaim: SELF_VERIFYING_DISTRIBUTION_PAYLOAD — withdrawn as overstated; the earlier wording implied the payload could vouch for itself
honest: An honest, unreplaced runner detects accidental drift. If the generated module, the manifest or diagnose.mjs itself is corrupted in transit, truncated, partially copied or edited by hand on one side only, the run refuses with one fixed code before the module is evaluated. That is the property this package actually delivers.

A replaced runner cannot self-authenticate. diagnose.mjs reads its own bytes from the payload and compares them with manifest.diagnostics, which sits in the same payload; anyone able to rewrite the module can rewrite the runner and the manifest digest together and the run will report healthy. Verification by a component of the artifact it verifies is circular and is not tamper-proof against a deliberate editor.

Only an external verifier makes the digest binding. The diagnostics digest becomes trustworthy exactly when a party outside the payload pins the expected sha256 for that exact payload out of band — a trusted publisher record, a registry entry or a release record — and compares it before running diagnose.mjs. No such external pin exists today, so the digest is currently a consistency check, not an authenticity check.
notClaimed: not tamper-proof, not tamper-resistant and not attested against a deliberate attacker who can rewrite the payload
not a signature, not a chain of trust and not a substitute for a signed release
not evidence that any external party ran it; no team consumed this payload

externalPin.howToUse: a party outside the payload records the expected manifest.diagnostics sha256 for one exact payload, then compares the shipped manifest against that recorded value before invoking diagnose.mjs
externalPin.pinnedToday: nothing. No concrete manifest.diagnostics value is pinned anywhere today — not in this planning record, not in the CHANGELOG entry, not in any registry, release record or distribution channel. externalPin.whyNoSingleValueCanBePinnedHere: the digest is not one constant. It is derived per payload from schemaVersion, distributionVersion, coordinate, integrity, diagnosticsPath and diagnosticsSource, so it varies with the contract and the distributionVersion passed to renderConsumerDiagnosticsDistribution. Any single value written into this record would be wrong for every other payload
externalPin.deliveredHere: this package makes the exact value derivable and observable, and nothing more: the runner bytes are one constant in the generator, the digest key order is fixed, and manifest.diagnostics is emitted in every payload, so the expected digest for a given payload can be recomputed deterministically and read off
externalPin.stillRequired: a future trusted publisher, registry or release record must pin the exact digest for each payload out of band before diagnose.mjs is invoked. Until that exists there is no external pin, and the honest claim above stands unreduced
